title: He saw a miracle, and it made him ask for one.
subtitle: Zakariyya's prayer in old age
then: Ibn Kathir explains that when Zakariyya saw Allah provide for Maryam out of season, {idea}he became eager for a child of his own{/idea}. He was old with grey hair, and his wife was barren. Still, he called on Allah in secret.
now: Your friend's prayer gets answered: the visa, the baby, the cure. A quiet voice says yours is too far gone. {idea}Zakariyya let someone else's miracle make him braver, not jealous.{/idea}
old: Some things are too late for me to even ask for.
new: If Allah gives out of season for others, I can ask Him too.
try: Make dua today for the one thing you stopped asking for.

title: The answer came while he was still praying.
subtitle: Glad tidings of Yahya
then: The angels called him while he stood in prayer. Ibn Kathir notes the name Yahya means he lives, since {reward}Allah filled his life with faith{/reward}. Many early scholars said he would believe in Isa, the Word from Allah. The news that he would be a prophet was better still.
now: You ask for a job and get a job with people who make you better. You ask for a child and get a child who teaches you patience. {reward}Allah's answers often come bigger than the request.{/reward}
old: If I get exactly what I asked for, I will be happy.
new: Allah can answer with more than I knew to ask for.
try: Stay in your prayer place for one extra minute after salah today and make dua.

title: How? Allah does what He wills.
subtitle: When the good news sounds impossible
then: Hearing the good news, Zakariyya wondered how it could happen at his age with a barren wife. Ibn Kathir explains the reply: {idea}this is Allah's matter, He is so mighty that nothing escapes His power.{/idea}
now: The doctor gave you the numbers. The bank said no. Your mind keeps listing the reasons it cannot happen. {idea}It is fine to ask how.{/idea} {reward}Just remember who you are asking.{/reward}
old: The facts say it cannot happen, so it will not.
new: Facts bind me, not Allah. He does what He wills.
try: Write down one thing you think is impossible, and under it write: Allah does what He wills.

title: Three days of silence, filled with remembrance.
subtitle: The sign given to Zakariyya
then: Zakariyya asked for a sign that the child was coming. Ibn Kathir explains he would {idea}not be able to speak except by signals, though he was not mute{/idea}. And he was told to remember his Lord much and glorify Him morning and evening.
now: You lose your voice, or your phone breaks, or you are stuck in a waiting room for hours. {reward}A forced pause can be the best time for dhikr.{/reward} Zakariyya could not talk to people, but he could talk to Allah.
old: When I cannot do my usual things, the time is lost.
new: A quiet stretch is a chance to remember Allah more.
try: Spend five minutes in silence today saying subhanAllah, with your phone in another room.

title: Chosen, purified, and chosen again.
subtitle: The angels speak to Maryam
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah chose Maryam {idea}because of her service to Him, her modesty, honor, and conviction{/idea}. He cites the hadith that the best woman of her time was Maryam, and of the Prophet's ﷺ time, Khadijah.
now: Nobody at work notices your quiet prayers in the stairwell. Nobody tags you for keeping your dignity. {reward}Maryam was chosen above the women of the worlds for exactly that kind of hidden devotion.{/reward}
old: Quiet devotion does not get noticed.
new: Allah notices and honors the hidden service of His servants.
try: Do one act of worship today that only Allah will see.

title: Honored? Then pray more.
subtitle: What Maryam was told to do with her honor
then: Right after telling her she was chosen, the angels told her to worship more. Ibn Kathir explains this was so she could carry {idea}what Allah had decreed for her as a test{/idea}, a son without a father, which earned her a higher grade in this life and the next.
now: You got the good news: the acceptance letter, the engagement, the new role. {idea}That is exactly when you need more prayer, not less.{/idea} Blessings come with tests attached.
old: When things go well, I can ease off worship.
new: Honor and blessing are reasons to bow lower and pray more.
try: After your next piece of good news, pray two extra rakat of thanks.

title: You were not there. Allah told you.
subtitle: The lots cast for Maryam's care
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ikrimah and others that the scholars of the masjid each wanted to care for Maryam, seeking reward. {idea}They threw their pens into the river{/idea}, and only Zakariyya's stayed in place. The Prophet ﷺ was not there; Allah revealed it to him.
now: Think of the people who once competed to do good for you: the aunt who wanted to raise you, the teacher who stayed late. {reward}Being cared for is its own blessing.{/reward} {idea}So is competing to care for others.{/idea}
old: People only compete for money and positions.
new: The best people compete to take care of others, for Allah's reward.
try: Volunteer for one caring task today before anyone else claims it.

title: A Word from Allah, named the Messiah, son of Mary.
subtitle: The good news of Isa
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa came into being with a word from Allah: Be. He was called the Messiah because {reward}those he touched were healed by Allah's leave{/reward}, and named after his mother because {idea}he had no father{/idea}. He would be honored and among those near to Allah.
now: Your Christian neighbor asks what Muslims believe about Jesus. You might be surprised how much you can say. {reward}He is honored, near to Allah, a Word from Him.{/reward} He also has a mother whose name he carries.
old: Isa belongs to another religion's story.
new: Isa is honored in my own faith, a servant brought near to Allah.
try: Learn one thing the Quran says about Isa, so you can share it kindly if asked.

title: A baby speaks, and a man speaks the same message.
subtitle: Isa in the cradle and in maturity
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa called to the worship of Allah alone {idea}while still in the cradle, as a miracle{/idea}, and again as a man by revelation. He cites the hadith that only a few infants ever spoke in the cradle, Isa among them. He would be one of the righteous.
now: At twenty you were sure of your faith. At forty, the job and the mortgage blur it. {idea}Isa's message as a baby and as a man was the same.{/idea} Your core can stay steady while your life changes.
old: Faith naturally changes as I get older and busier.
new: My circumstances change, but what I call to can stay the same.
try: Recall what first made you feel close to Allah, and do that thing once this week.

title: Be, and it is.
subtitle: Maryam's question and Allah's answer
then: Maryam asked how she could have a son when no man had touched her. Ibn Kathir notes the angel said Allah {idea}creates{/idea}, rather than does as with Zakariyya, to remove any doubt about Isa. {reward}What Allah wills comes into existence instantly.{/reward}
now: You have a plan with fourteen steps and you are stuck on step two. {idea}Your steps matter, but they are not the limit.{/idea} The One you pray to does not need steps.
old: Things can only happen the normal way, one step at a time.
new: When Allah decrees something, He says Be, and it is.
try: Bring your hardest problem to Allah in dua today, without explaining how He should solve it.

title: He would be taught writing, wisdom, Torah and Gospel.
subtitle: What Allah would teach Isa
then: Ibn Kathir says the good news to Maryam was even greater because {reward}Allah would teach Isa writing and wisdom{/reward}, and both the Torah and the Gospel. He notes Isa memorized both books.
now: You read something that finally makes sense, or a skill clicks after months of practice. {idea}Every bit of knowledge is taught.{/idea} Even a prophet's learning came from Allah.
old: What I know, I figured out myself.
new: Whatever I learn is taught to me by Allah.
try: Before you study or read today, say: Rabbi zidni ilma, my Lord, increase me in knowledge.

title: Every miracle came with the words: by Allah's permission.
subtitle: The signs of Isa
then: Ibn Kathir notes scholars said every prophet got a miracle suited to his time. Musa came when magic was prized; {idea}Isa came when medicine was advancing{/idea}, and no physician could do what he did. Each sign was {reward}by Allah's leave{/reward}, proof of who sent him.
now: Your surgery goes well and you thank the surgeon. You should. {idea}And you can remember the permission behind it.{/idea} Even Isa repeated it, every time.
old: Talented people make good things happen on their own.
new: Every skill and success works by Allah's permission.
try: When you thank someone today, also say alhamdulillah in your heart.

title: He came to confirm, and to ease some burdens.
subtitle: Isa's mission to the Children of Israel
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa affirmed the Torah and {reward}made lawful part of what had been forbidden{/reward}, clearing up some of their disputes. He then said, as the next verse continues, that {idea}Allah is my Lord and your Lord{/idea}, equal in servitude to Him.
now: A good teacher does not want you to worship them. They point past themselves. {idea}Isa said obey me so that you would worship Allah.{/idea} The test of any guide is where they point you.
old: Following a good teacher means putting them on a pedestal.
new: The best guides point beyond themselves to Allah.
try: Thank a teacher who pointed you toward Allah, by message or in a dua.
